title: Realms Are Wrought by Karma and Manifested by the Mind
author: Zhanran (annotated)
excerpt: (The original text is recorded from the Collected Works of Master Chewu.)

inline.s: The original text is recorded from the Collected Works of Master Chewu

Realms are wrought by karma and manifested by the mind: every realm is entirely activated by karma and manifested by the mind. The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is activated by pure karma and manifested by a pure mind. Therefore, the practitioner
who recites the Buddha’s name with one mind and earnestly cultivates the pure karma
will certainly have the response of being reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

[One mind: mind after mind continuing unbroken, with no other thought intruding.] [Earnestly cultivating the pure karma: regarding the wondrous fruit of earnest cultivation of pure karma, Master Chewu instructed:
At
the time of reciting the Buddha’s name, one must let go of the ten thousand conditions and lift up single-mindedly
(the thought of Buddha-recitation)

the one. Like saving one’s head from burning, like mourning one’s parents, like a hen brooding her eggs, like a dragon nurturing its pearl—not expecting small benefits, not seeking quick success, but only always reciting thus with one mind; this is the supreme, deep, and wondrous Chan. If so, then the future body-mind and world, secretly following the mind,
are all being transformed thought after thought

. This is not something the common mind and fleshly eyes can know and see. Only when the retribution ends and life is done, and Amitābha Buddha with the host of sages suddenly appears before one—or there arise the strange fragrance, heavenly music, and all the auspicious signs—then the world says the pure karma has been accomplished. Yet the accomplishment of the pure karma—where does it occur at this very moment?
(The original text is found in
“Free and Spontaneous Rebirth”,
one article)

[Root-body: the body formed by the six faculties (eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind) combined.] [The various auspicious signs: Master Chewu himself, fully ten months before his rebirth, already knew the time of its coming, and the auspicious signs of his rebirth appeared in abundance.]

[All realms are activated only by karma and manifested only by the mind. In the very place where they manifest, the essence is the mind itself. Wherever there is a mind, there can be no absence of realms. If it does not manifest the Buddha-realm, it manifests the realms of the nine worlds. If it does not manifest the realms of the three vehicles, it manifests the realms of the six ordinary beings. If it does not manifest the realms of gods, humans, ghosts, and beasts, it manifests the hell-realm.]

All realms are entirely activated by karma and manifested by the mind. And the realm manifested is itself the very mind. As long as there is a mind, there cannot be an absence of realm. If this mind does not manifest the Buddha-realm, it manifests the realms of the nine worlds (hell, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, humans, gods, sravakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas). If it does not manifest the realms of the three vehicles (the vehicle of sravakas, the vehicle of pratyekabuddhas, the vehicle of bodhisattvas), it manifests the realms of the six ordinary beings (that is, the six courses, for all six courses are ordinary beings, hence called the six ordinary ones). If it does not manifest the realms of gods, humans, ghosts, and beasts, it manifests the hell realm.

[The realms manifested by the Buddha and the three vehicles, though they differ in excellence and inferiority, all enjoy only the bliss of the Dharma. The realms manifested by the gods of the three worlds enjoy only the bliss of meditative concentration and the five desires. The realm of the human way, with suffering and joy alternating, varies in measure according to one’s karma. The realms of ghosts and beasts have more suffering and less joy. As for hell, it is entirely extreme suffering.]

The realms manifested by the mind of the Buddha and the three vehicles, though they differ in excellence and inferiority, are, importantly, all enjoying the bliss of the Dharma. The realms manifested by the minds of the gods of the three worlds all enjoy the bliss of meditative concentration and the five desires. The realm manifested by the mind in the human way has both suffering and joy, varying in degree according to each person’s karmic retribution. The realms manifested by the minds of hungry ghosts and beasts have more suffering and less joy. As for the realm manifested by the mind in hell, it is entirely extreme suffering.

[Three worlds: the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.] [Five desires: form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. Form refers to beautiful appearances; sound refers to sweet tones; smell refers to fragrant scents; taste refers to delicious flavors; touch refers to pleasant sensations. These five are called the five desires because they cause people to give rise to a mind of greed and desire.]

[As with the mountains, rivers, people, and things one sees in a dream, all are manifested by the dreaming mind. If there were no dreaming mind, there would certainly be no dream-realm. And supposing there were no dream-realm, there would also be no dreaming mind. Therefore know that outside the mind there is no realm, and outside the realm there is no mind. The whole realm is the mind, and the whole mind is the realm. If one is to discern the fruit within the cause, one should contemplate the mind; if one is to verify the cause at the place of the fruit, one should contemplate the realm. Hence it is said: there is never a realm without a mind, nor ever a mind without a realm. The fruit must follow from the cause, and the cause must realize the fruit. If one truly knew this principle of the non-duality of mind-and-realm and cause-and-fruit, and still did not recite the Buddha’s name seeking rebirth in the Pure Land, I would not believe it.]

This is like the mountains, rivers, people, and things seen in a dream, all manifested by the dreaming mind. If there were no dreaming mind, there would surely be no dream-realm. And supposing there were no dream-realm, there would also be no dreaming mind. Therefore we know: outside the mind there is no realm, and outside the realm there is no mind. The realm is the mind, and the mind is the realm. If one examines (knows) the fruit within the cause, one must contemplate the mind; if one verifies (examines) the cause at the place of the fruit, one should contemplate the realm. Hence it is said: there is no realm without a mind, and no mind without a realm. The fruit must come from the cause, and the cause must manifest as the fruit. If one truly knew this principle of the non-duality of mind and realm, and of cause and fruit, and still did not recite the Buddha’s name seeking rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, I absolutely would not believe it!
[One Suchness: not two and not different is called One Suchness.]
